title: Ensure Passwords are Set for All OceanBase Accounts
description: If any account exists without a password (i.e., a null-password account), it reduces the attack cost-attackers only need to guess the username correctly to gain access without requiring a password. Therefore, it is essential to ensure that all OceanBase accounts are configured with passwords to prevent unauthorized malicious users from accessing the database. Runs obclient with the connection options in OB_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys"); point it at the MySQL-mode tenant being assessed and supply the password via OB_CONN (-p...) or a [client] section in ~/.my.cnf. Passes when neither mysql.user nor oceanbase.__all_user contains an account with an empty password.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.1 Ensure Passwords are Set for All OceanBase Accounts

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys} -N -B -e "SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE LENGTH(password) = 0) + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM oceanbase.__all_user WHERE LENGTH(passwd) = 0)" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: SET PASSWORD FOR <user> = PASSWORD('<strong password>'); for every account returned.

title: Ensure Passwords are Set for All Accounts
description: Blank passwords allow a user to login without using a password. Oracle-mode tenant. Passes when no user in SYS.DBA_USERS has a NULL password; also confirm no account keeps a default password. Runs obclient against an Oracle-mode tenant using the connection options in OB_ORA_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uSYS@oracle"); supply the password via OB_ORA_CONN (-p...) or ~/.my.cnf.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1.6 Ensure Passwords are Set for All Accounts

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_ORA_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uSYS@oracle} -N -B -e "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SYS.DBA_USERS WHERE PASSWORD IS NULL" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: ALTER USER <username> IDENTIFIED BY <strong password>; for every user returned.

title: Ensure 'data_dir' Has Appropriate Permissions
description: The cluster-level configuration parameter 'data_dir' displays the directory for storing data such as SSTables. Currently, it is read-only and cannot be modified.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3 Ensure 'data_dir' Has Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: Run SELECT svr_ip, name, value FROM oceanbase.GV$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name = 'data_dir'; then on each host ls -ld <data_dir> (ls -ldL if it is a symlink; default /home/admin/oceanbase/store). The directory must be mode 750 (drwxr-x---) or stricter and owned by the admin user and group; any world access or other owner is a finding.

remediation.command: To remediate incorrect permissions or ownership on the OceanBase data directory: 1. Confirm the current permissions and ownership: ls -ld /data/1 2. Set the correct ownership to the admin user and group: sudo chown admin:admin /data/1 3. Restrict permissions to owner read/write/execute and group read/execute only: sudo chmod 750 /data/1 4. Verify the change: ls -ld /data/1 Expected output: drwxr-x--- 10 admin admin 4096 Jan 1 10:00 /data/1

title: Use Dedicated Least Privileged Account for OceanBase Daemon/Service
description: As with any service installed on a host, it can be provided with its own user context. Providing a dedicated user to the service provides the ability to precisely constrain the service within the larger host context. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when every observer process runs as a non-root account (FAIL when none is running); also confirm the account (default admin) is dedicated to OceanBase and not a shared interactive login.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4 Use Dedicated Least Privileged Account for OceanBase Daemon/Service

audit.command: out=$(ps -eo user=,comm= 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$2 == "observer" {n++; if ($1 == "root") r++} END {if (n == 0) print "not running"; else if (r > 0) print "root"; else print "compliant"}'

remediation.command: Create a dedicated non-login service account (default admin), chown the OceanBase home, data_dir and log directories to it and restart observer under that account (via OBD/OCP or the service unit).

title: Ensure the Appropriate Version for OceanBase Software Is Installed
description: The OceanBase installation version should be the most recent that are compatible with the organization's operational needs.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1 Ensure the Appropriate Version for OceanBase Software Is Installed

audit.command: Run SELECT ob_version(); and compare the result with the OceanBase Product Lifecycle page: the current date must be before the End of Standard Support (or End of Extended Support) date of that version, preferably an LTS release on its latest patch. An EOL version is a finding.

remediation.command: Perform the following steps for remediation: 1. Identify the target version: - Check the Release Notes to find the latest LTS (Long Term Support) version or the latest compatible patch version. 2. Download and apply the upgrade: - Download the installation package for the target version. - Upgrade the observer using the OceanBase Control Platform (OCP) or your standard upgrade procedure.

title: Backup Strategy in Place
description: A backup strategy should be in place.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.1 Backup Strategy in Place

audit.command: Verify that a backup strategy exists and is actively configured for OceanBase tenants: - If OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP) is used, review the backup policies and schedules configured in OCP for each production tenant. Confirm that backups are scheduled at an appropriate frequency (e.g., daily) and that recent successful backup jobs are recorded in the OCP job history.

remediation.command: Establish a formal backup strategy aligned with business continuity requirements: - Define backup scope (which tenants/databases), frequency, retention period, and storage location. - If using OCP, configure automated backup policies through the platform's backup management interface. - If not using OCP, implement and document a repeatable backup procedure using supported OceanBase tools, and schedule it via cron or orchestration systems.

title: Limit Accepted Transport Layer Security (TLS) Versions
description: OceanBase supports multiple protocols of TLS. The higher the version the stronger the security and/or better the performance. Runs obclient with the connection options in OB_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys"); point it at the MySQL-mode tenant being assessed and supply the password via OB_CONN (-p...) or a [client] section in ~/.my.cnf. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when sql_protocol_min_tls_version is TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.3 on every OBServer (unset/none, TLSv1 or TLSv1.1 fail).
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.2.1 Limit Accepted Transport Layer Security (TLS) Versions

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys} -N -B -e "SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN value IN ('TLSv1.2', 'TLSv1.3') THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) = 0 THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END FROM oceanbase.GV\$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name = 'sql_protocol_min_tls_version'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET sql_protocol_min_tls_version = 'TLSv1.2';

title: Only Approved Servers can Access
description: Specify an allowlist of approved servers that can access to the cluster. Runs obclient with the connection options in OB_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys"); point it at the MySQL-mode tenant being assessed and supply the password via OB_CONN (-p...) or a [client] section in ~/.my.cnf. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when _ob_ssl_invited_nodes is a non-empty, explicit list of trusted IPs/hosts on every OBServer (empty, None, ALL or 0.0.0.0/0 fail).
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.2.2 Only Approved Servers can Access

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys} -N -B -e "SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN value IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(value) <> '' AND UPPER(value) NOT IN ('ALL', 'NONE') AND value NOT LIKE '%0.0.0.0/0%' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) = 0 THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END FROM oceanbase.GV\$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name = '_ob_ssl_invited_nodes'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET _ob_ssl_invited_nodes = '<ip1>,<ip2>,...'; listing only the application servers, OCP nodes and backup servers that need TLS connectivity.

title: Limit Accepted TLS Versions
description: OceanBase supports communication encryption to ensure that traffic between nodes cannot be eavesdropped or tampered with. Runs obclient with the connection options in OB_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys"); point it at the MySQL-mode tenant being assessed and supply the password via OB_CONN (-p...) or a [client] section in ~/.my.cnf. Passes when sql_protocol_min_tls_version is TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.3 on all OBServer nodes (none, any, TLSv1 or TLSv1.1 fail). Mismatched values across nodes fail because each row is checked.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.2.3 Limit Accepted TLS Versions

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys} -N -B -e "SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN value IN ('TLSv1.2', 'TLSv1.3') THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) = 0 THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END FROM oceanbase.GV\$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name = 'sql_protocol_min_tls_version'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET sql_protocol_min_tls_version = 'TLSv1.2'; (or 'TLSv1.3') and confirm the value on every OBServer with SHOW PARAMETERS LIKE 'sql_protocol_min_tls_version';

title: Ensure Replication Traffic is Secured
description: The replication traffic between servers in OceanBase cluster should be secured. Security measures should include ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of the traffic, and performing mutual authentication between the servers before performing replication. Runs obclient with the connection options in OB_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys"); point it at the MySQL-mode tenant being assessed and supply the password via OB_CONN (-p...) or a [client] section in ~/.my.cnf. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when ssl_client_authentication is True and rpc_server_authentication_method is SSL_NO_ENCRYPT on every OBServer; also confirm valid certificates are deployed on all observers.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.3 Ensure Replication Traffic is Secured

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys} -N -B -e "SELECT CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN name = 'ssl_client_authentication' AND UPPER(value) = 'TRUE' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN name = 'ssl_client_authentication' AND UPPER(value) <> 'TRUE' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN name = 'rpc_server_authentication_method' AND UPPER(value) = 'SSL_NO_ENCRYPT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN name = 'rpc_server_authentication_method' AND UPPER(value) <> 'SSL_NO_ENCRYPT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END FROM oceanbase.GV\$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name IN ('ssl_client_authentication', 'rpc_server_authentication_method')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Deploy CA/server certificates to every observer, then ALTER SYSTEM SET ssl_client_authentication = 'True'; ALTER SYSTEM SET rpc_server_authentication_method = 'SSL_NO_ENCRYPT'; and set sql_protocol_min_tls_version = 'TLSv1.2'.

title: Ensure No Users Have Wildcard Hostnames
description: All user accounts in the database should be strictly restricted to connect only from specific hosts or IP addresses explicitly required for their business operations. Runs obclient with the connection options in OB_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys"); point it at the MySQL-mode tenant being assessed and supply the password via OB_CONN (-p...) or a [client] section in ~/.my.cnf. Passes when no account has host '%' (the defaults root@% and ORAAUDITOR@% fail until restricted).
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.7 Ensure No Users Have Wildcard Hostnames

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys} -N -B -e "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE host = '%'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: RENAME USER '<user>'@'%' TO '<user>'@'<approved host or subnet>'; for every account returned.

title: Ensure 'CREATE USER' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
description: The "CREATE USER" privilege controls the ability of a specific user to add or delete users, modify existing usernames, and revoke permissions from existing users. Runs obclient with the connection options in OB_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys"); point it at the MySQL-mode tenant being assessed and supply the password via OB_CONN (-p...) or a [client] section in ~/.my.cnf. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when no non-root grantee holds CREATE USER.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2.1 Ensure 'CREATE USER' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys} -N -B -e "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.user_privileges WHERE GRANTEE NOT LIKE '''root''%' AND PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'CREATE USER'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: REVOKE CREATE USER ON *.* FROM '<user>';

title: Ensure 'SUPER' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
description: The SUPER privilege determines whether a user can perform certain powerful administrative functions, including terminating user sessions via the KILL command, modifying global MySQL variables using SET GLOBAL, and executing various commands related to replication and logging. Runs obclient with the connection options in OB_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys"); point it at the MySQL-mode tenant being assessed and supply the password via OB_CONN (-p...) or a [client] section in ~/.my.cnf. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when no non-root grantee holds SUPER.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2.3 Ensure 'SUPER' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys} -N -B -e "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.user_privileges WHERE GRANTEE NOT LIKE '''root''%' AND PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'SUPER'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: REVOKE SUPER ON *.* FROM '<user>';

title: Use TDE for At-Rest Data Encryption
description: OceanBase supports table-granularity transparent encryption to achieve secure data storage. Runs obclient with the connection options in OB_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys"); point it at the MySQL-mode tenant being assessed and supply the password via OB_CONN (-p...) or a [client] section in ~/.my.cnf. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when tde_method is not none (e.g. internal or bkmi) on every OBServer for the tenant.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.3.1 Use TDE for At-Rest Data Encryption

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys} -N -B -e "SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(value) <> 'none' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) = 0 THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END FROM oceanbase.GV\$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name = 'tde_method'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET tde_method = 'internal'; (or a KMS-backed method), confirm with SHOW PARAMETERS LIKE 'tde_method'; then create encrypted tablespaces / tables for sensitive data.

title: Ensure ALL Events are Audited
description: The database audit function must record all critical operations to support security incident traceability, compliance reviews, and behavioral analysis. Runs obclient with the connection options in OB_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys"); point it at the MySQL-mode tenant being assessed and supply the password via OB_CONN (-p...) or a [client] section in ~/.my.cnf. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when audit_trail is not None (DB, DB,EXTENDED, DB_EXTENDED or OS) for the tenant on every server.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.4.1 Ensure ALL Events are Audited

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys} -N -B -e "SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN UPPER(value) <> 'NONE' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) = 0 THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END FROM oceanbase.GV\$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name = 'audit_trail'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET audit_trail = 'DB_EXTENDED'; and on 4.2.4+ apply an audit filter: SELECT AUDIT_LOG_FILTER_SET_FILTER('log_all', '{"filter": {"log": true}}'); SELECT AUDIT_LOG_FILTER_SET_USER('%', 'log_all');

title: Public Role Privileges
description: The unnecessary privileges should be revoked from default public role to minimize security risks and adhere to the principle of least privilege. Oracle-mode tenant. Passes when PUBLIC holds no system, role or object privileges; any grant that is returned must be justified by organisational need. Runs obclient against an Oracle-mode tenant using the connection options in OB_ORA_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uSYS@oracle"); supply the password via OB_ORA_CONN (-p...) or ~/.my.cnf.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.2.1 Public Role Privileges

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_ORA_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uSYS@oracle} -N -B -e "SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM DBA_SYS_PRIVS WHERE GRANTEE = 'PUBLIC') + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM DBA_ROLE_PRIVS WHERE GRANTEE = 'PUBLIC') + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM USER_TAB_PRIVS WHERE GRANTEE = 'PUBLIC') FROM DUAL" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: REVOKE <role> FROM PUBLIC; REVOKE <system_privilege> FROM PUBLIC; REVOKE <privilege> ON <object> FROM PUBLIC; for every unnecessary grant.

title: Only Allowed Client can Access to Cluster
description: Specify an client whitelist of approved servers that can access to the cluster. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Oracle-mode tenant. Passes when ob_tcp_invited_nodes is an explicit IP list rather than '%'. Runs obclient against an Oracle-mode tenant using the connection options in OB_ORA_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uSYS@oracle"); supply the password via OB_ORA_CONN (-p...) or ~/.my.cnf.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.2.3 Only Allowed Client can Access to Cluster

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_ORA_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uSYS@oracle} -N -B -e "SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'ob_tcp_invited_nodes'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk -F'\t' '$1 == "ob_tcp_invited_nodes" {v = $2; f = 1} END {gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", v); print (f && v != "" && v != "%") ? "compliant" : "noncompliant"}'

remediation.command: SET GLOBAL ob_tcp_invited_nodes = '<ip list>'; containing only the approved client addresses.

title: Use TDE for At-Rest Data Encryption
description: Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) at-rest encryption protects your critical data by enabling data-at-rest encryption in the database. It protects the privacy of your information, prevents data breaches and helps meet regulatory requirements.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.3.1 Use TDE for At-Rest Data Encryption

audit.command: In the Oracle-mode tenant run SELECT TABLE_NAME, ENCRYPTED FROM V$OB_ENCRYPTED_TABLES; Tables holding sensitive data must be listed with ENCRYPTED = YES; no rows, or NO for a table that requires at-rest encryption, is a finding.

remediation.command: Remediate this setting by executing the following SQL statements to enable TDE for tables according to the organization requirements: 1. Create a tablespace and specify the encryption algorithm. CREATE TABLESPACE <tablespace_name> ENCRYPTION USING '<encryption algorithm>' 2. Move the unencrypted table to the tablespace. ALTER TALBE <table_name> TABLESPACE <tablespace_name>; 3. Perform a full compaction on the table.

title: Ensure 'AUDIT_TRAIL' is not set to NONE
description: The audit_trail setting determines whether or not OceanBase's basic audit features are enabled. It can be set to OS(Operating System); DB; DB_EXTENDED; or DB, EXTENDED. The value should be set according to the needs of the organization. NONE means audit is disabled. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Oracle-mode tenant, using the benchmark query. Passes when audit_trail is OS, DB, DB_EXTENDED or DB,EXTENDED on every server. Runs obclient against an Oracle-mode tenant using the connection options in OB_ORA_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uSYS@oracle"); supply the password via OB_ORA_CONN (-p...) or ~/.my.cnf.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.1 Ensure 'AUDIT_TRAIL' is not set to NONE

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_ORA_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uSYS@oracle} -N -B -e "SELECT svr_ip, name, value FROM oceanbase.GV\$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name = 'audit_trail'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk -F'\t' 'NF >= 3 {n++; v = toupper($3); if (v != "OS" && v != "DB" && v != "DB_EXTENDED" && v != "DB,EXTENDED") b++} END {print (n > 0 && b == 0) ? "compliant" : "noncompliant"}'

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET AUDIT_TRAIL = 'DB_EXTENDED'; (or OS / DB / 'DB,EXTENDED' per policy).

title: Place Databases on Non-System Partitions
description: It is generally accepted that host operating systems should include different filesystem partitions for different purposes. One set of filesystems is typically called system partitions, and these are generally reserved for host system/application operation. The other set of filesystems is typically called "non-system partitions", and such locations are generally reserved for storing data.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1 Place Databases on Non-System Partitions

audit.command: Use the following procedure to assess compliance: 1. Connect to the OceanBase database as an administrative user and run: SELECT svr_ip, name, value FROM oceanbase.GV$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name = 'data_dir'; 2. For each returned value (e.g., /data/1), determine its filesystem mount point by running: df -h <datadir>/sstable 3. Examine the "Mounted on" column in the output. This recommendation is compliant if the filesystem mounted at the OceanBase data_dir path (and any associated subdirectories such as log or sstable directories) is not the root (/), /var, or /usr filesystem.

remediation.command: Perform the following steps to remediate this setting for the datadir: 1. Backup the database. 2. Choose a non-system partition new location for OceanBase data files. 3. Stop observer using a command like: pkill -9 observer. 4. Copy the data using a command like: cp -rp <datadir> <new location>. 5. Delete datadir and create a symlink instead to point to the new location using a command like: ln -s <new location> <datadir> 6. Restart observer.

title: Ensure the Partition Size for Log Files is Large Enough
description: The database files and directories should place to a non-system partition and the partition size should be large enough. For OceanBase stable running and accommondating log growth, the partition size for OceanBase log files must have at least 3-4 times the available memory .
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2 Ensure the Partition Size for Log Files is Large Enough

audit.command: Run SELECT svr_ip, name, value FROM oceanbase.GV$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name IN ('data_dir','memory_limit','memory_limit_percentage'); Derive available memory (memory_limit, or memory_limit_percentage x MemTotal from /proc/meminfo). For each log directory (e.g. /data/log1, df -h <dir>) the partition must be at least 3-4 times the observer available memory; a smaller log partition is a finding.

remediation.command: Assume the disk used for the log partition is large enough. Then perform the following steps to remediate this setting for the log directory: 1. Backup the database. 2. Stop observer using a command like: pkill -9 observer. 3. Dismount the log partition usming command like: umount /data/log1. 4. Resize the log partition and the filesystem. 5. Mount the log partition to the original directory: mount <partition> /data/log1. 6. Restart observer. 7.

title: Use OceanBase Official Signed Installation Packages
description: OceanBase official release packages are signed with a GPG key. Before using the packages, users can verify their integrity by checking the signature, thereby preventing supply chain poisoning attacks caused by tampered or untrusted installation packages.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.2 Use OceanBase Official Signed Installation Packages

audit.command: For environments deployed using the OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP), verify that installation packages are sourced exclusively from official OceanBase channels and that OCP's built-in signature validation mechanism is enabled. Review deployment logs or audit records from OCP to confirm that no unsigned or untrusted packages were installed. The presence of alerts or rejection events related to package signature validation indicates that the control is active.

remediation.command: Ensure that all OceanBase installation packages used in production environments are obtained directly from official OceanBase distribution channels and bear valid digital signatures issued by OceanBase. Coordinate with authorized OceanBase support or delivery personnel to confirm the authenticity and integrity of software packages prior to deployment.

title: Configure Alert Threshold for Unexpected Backup Events
description: An alert should be triggered when the unexpected backup events occur such as data backup timeout, log backup delay or no successful data backup in many days.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.3 Configure Alert Threshold for Unexpected Backup Events

audit.command: Review the backup alert configuration for each OceanBase tenant to confirm that meaningful thresholds are defined and aligned with organizational requirements: - If OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP) is used, examine the tenant-level backup policy settings and verify that alert thresholds are configured for the following conditions: o Data backup timeout o Log backup delay o Consecutive days without a successful data backup - Confirm that the configured thresholds reflect the organization's operational needs-for example, the "days without backup" threshold should not exceed the backup ...

remediation.command: Configure or adjust backup alert thresholds to ensure timely notification of failures: - In OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP), update the tenant's backup strategy to define appropriate alert thresholds based on observed backup behavior and business requirements. o For Data Backup Timeout, set the threshold to a value greater than the typical completion time of recent successful backups (e.g., 1.5× average duration).

title: Point-in-Time Recovery
description: With clogs it is possible to implement point-in-time recovery. This makes it possible to restore the changes between the last full backup and the point-in-time. The clogs need to be backed up with data backup. The restore procedure should be created and tested.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.4 Point-in-Time Recovery

audit.command: Verify that clog (log) backup is enabled and that a restore procedure exists: - If OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP) is used, review the tenant-level backup configuration and confirm that log backup is explicitly enabled as part of the backup strategy. - Additionally, examine operational documentation or disaster recovery plans to confirm that a point-in-time recovery procedure has been defined and tested within the past 12 months (or per organizational policy).

remediation.command: Enable clog backup and establish a recovery validation process: - In OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP), modify the tenant's backup policy to enable the Log Backup feature. Ensure the log backup destination is reliable and monitored. - Develop a formal point-in-time recovery procedure that outlines how to restore from a full backup and replay clogs to a specified timestamp.

title: Verify Backups are Good
description: Backups should be validated on a regular basis.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.5 Verify Backups are Good

audit.command: Review evidence that backup validation is performed systematically: - Examine backup validation or recovery test reports from the past 12 months (or per organizational policy). These may include: o Test plans and execution records from OceanBase Control Platform (OCP) recovery sampling tasks; o Screenshots, logs, or audit trails showing successful restore operations; o Post-test summaries confirming data consistency and application functionality. - If OCP is used, confirm that recovery sampling tasks are configured and have executed successfully within the review period.

remediation.command: Establish a formal backup validation program: - Implement regular recovery sampling tasks via OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP), scheduled at intervals aligned with business risk (e.g., quarterly for critical systems). - Ensure each test includes: o Restoration of a representative tenant or dataset; o Verification of data completeness and consistency; o Validation that applications can operate correctly on the restored data.

title: Disable creating accounts via the GRANT statement
description: When using the GRANT statement, if the target user does not exist, the system will attempt to create the user. This may lead to unintentional creation of a user with an empty password when the GRANT statement contains errors, introducing account management risks. Enabling the NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER setting in the sql_mode configuration option can prevent the GRANT statement from creating users. Runs obclient with the connection options in OB_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys"); point it at the MySQL-mode tenant being assessed and supply the password via OB_CONN (-p...) or a [client] section in ~/.my.cnf. Passes when the global sql_mode contains NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER (new sessions inherit it).
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.2 Disable creating accounts via the GRANT statement

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys} -N -B -e "SELECT CASE WHEN FIND_IN_SET('NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER', @@global.sql_mode) > 0 THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: SET @@global.sql_mode = CONCAT(@@global.sql_mode, ',NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER'); (as a user with SUPER).

title: Ensure Password Complexity Policies are in Place
description: OceanBase MySQL tenants support configuring password complexity policies through tenant-level system variables. Enabling password complexity policies helps prevent weak password usage and raises the bar for password cracking. Runs obclient with the connection options in OB_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys"); point it at the MySQL-mode tenant being assessed and supply the password via OB_CONN (-p...) or a [client] section in ~/.my.cnf. Passes when validate_password_length >= 14, validate_password_check_user_name = ON, validate_password_policy = MEDIUM (or stronger) and the mixed-case, number and special-character counts are each >= 1.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.3 Ensure Password Complexity Policies are in Place

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys} -N -B -e "SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'validate_password%'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk -F'\t' '{v[$1] = toupper($2)} END {ok = (v["validate_password_length"] + 0 >= 14 && v["validate_password_check_user_name"] == "ON" && (v["validate_password_policy"] == "MEDIUM" || v["validate_password_policy"] == "STRONG") && v["validate_password_mixed_case_count"] + 0 >= 1 && v["validate_password_number_count"] + 0 >= 1 && v["validate_password_special_char_count"] + 0 >= 1); print ok ? "compliant" : "noncompliant"}'

remediation.command: SET GLOBAL validate_password_length = 14; SET GLOBAL validate_password_check_user_name = ON; SET GLOBAL validate_password_policy = MEDIUM; SET GLOBAL validate_password_mixed_case_count = 1; SET GLOBAL validate_password_number_count = 1; SET GLOBAL validate_password_special_char_count = 1;

title: Do Not Reuse Usernames
description: Each database user account should be assigned a unique purpose (e.g., dedicated to a specific individual or application) and should not be shared among multiple different applications or users.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.4 Do Not Reuse Usernames

audit.command: This recommendation requires a manual review to map database accounts to real-world owners (applications or individuals) and to confirm that accounts are not shared. 1. Obtain a list of non-reserved (non-system) users: SELECT User, Host FROM mysql.user WHERE User NOT IN ('root','ORAAUDITOR','proxyro'); 2.

remediation.command: 1. List text hereCreate dedicated accounts for each application/user: CREATE USER 'app1_user'@'10.%' IDENTIFIED BY 'Strong_Password_Here'; CREATE USER 'app2_user'@'10.%' IDENTIFIED BY 'Strong_Password_Here'; 2. List text hereGrant only the required privileges (examples; adjust to your schema and least-privilege requirements): GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON app1_db.* TO 'app1_user'@'10.%'; GRANT SELECT ON app2_db.* TO 'app2_user'@'10.%';

title: Configure account locking after consecutive authentication failures
description: OceanBase MySQL tenants support using the tenant-level configuration parameter connection_control_failed_connections_threshold to specify the threshold for failed login attempts. Accounts exceeding this threshold will be locked, and the lock duration can be set via the parameters connection_control_min_connection_delay and connection_control_max_connection_delay. Runs obclient with the connection options in OB_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys"); point it at the MySQL-mode tenant being assessed and supply the password via OB_CONN (-p...) or a [client] section in ~/.my.cnf. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when connection_control_failed_connections_threshold is not 0 on every server; confirm the threshold (5 or fewer) and connection_control_min/max_connection_delay meet policy.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.5 Configure account locking after consecutive authentication failures

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys} -N -B -e "SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN value <> '0' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) = 0 THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END FROM oceanbase.GV\$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name = 'connection_control_failed_connections_threshold'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET connection_control_failed_connections_threshold = 5; and set connection_control_min_connection_delay / connection_control_max_connection_delay (milliseconds) per policy.

title: Set 'default_password_lifetime' to Require a Yearly Password Change
description: The system parameter default_password_lifetime can be used to configure the global password expiration period for OceanBase tenant users. After a password expires, it must be reset before any further operations can be performed. Configuring a password expiration period enhances operational security and system compliance, reducing the risks associated with password leakage. Runs obclient with the connection options in OB_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys"); point it at the MySQL-mode tenant being assessed and supply the password via OB_CONN (-p...) or a [client] section in ~/.my.cnf. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when default_password_lifetime is between 1 and 365 days (0 means passwords never expire).
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.6 Set 'default_password_lifetime' to Require a Yearly Password Change

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys} -N -B -e "SELECT CASE WHEN @@global.default_password_lifetime BETWEEN 1 AND 365 THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: SET GLOBAL default_password_lifetime = 365;

title: Ensure 'PROCESS' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
description: The "PROCESS" privilege controls whether a specified user can view the statement execution information of all sessions. Runs obclient with the connection options in OB_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys"); point it at the MySQL-mode tenant being assessed and supply the password via OB_CONN (-p...) or a [client] section in ~/.my.cnf. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when no non-root grantee holds PROCESS.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2.2 Ensure 'PROCESS' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys} -N -B -e "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.user_privileges WHERE GRANTEE NOT LIKE '''root''%' AND PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'PROCESS'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: REVOKE PROCESS ON *.* FROM '<user>';

title: Ensure AES Encryption Mode is Configured Correctly
description: When using AES_ENCRYPT() and AES_DECRYPT() functions for encryption, it is recommended to use block cipher encryption in Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode with a 256-bit key length. Runs obclient with the connection options in OB_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys"); point it at the MySQL-mode tenant being assessed and supply the password via OB_CONN (-p...) or a [client] section in ~/.my.cnf. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when block_encryption_mode is an AES-256 non-ECB mode (aes-256-cbc recommended); the default aes-128-ecb fails.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.3.2 Ensure AES Encryption Mode is Configured Correctly

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uroot@sys} -N -B -e "SELECT CASE WHEN LOWER(@@global.block_encryption_mode) LIKE 'aes-256-%' AND LOWER(@@global.block_encryption_mode) NOT LIKE '%ecb' THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: SET GLOBAL block_encryption_mode = 'aes-256-cbc';

title: Ensure Audit Filters Capture Connection Attempts
description: The functions audit_log_filter_set_filter and audit_log_filter_set_user are used to define audit rules, which can audit both successful and failed connection events and write them to the audit log file.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.4.2 Ensure Audit Filters Capture Connection Attempts

audit.command: Run SHOW PARAMETERS LIKE 'audit_trail'; (must not be None). Then review SELECT * FROM oceanbase.__all_tenant_security_audit_record ORDER BY gmt_create DESC LIMIT 20; and/or SELECT * FROM oceanbase.__all_tenant_user_failed_login_stat LIMIT 20; Connection and authentication attempts, including failures, must appear in the audit records; otherwise this is a finding.

remediation.command: For OceanBase 4.2.4 and later: SELECT AUDIT_LOG_FILTER_SET_FILTER( 'conn_attempt_filter', '{ "filter": { "log": true, "class": [ { "name": "connection" } ] } }' ); SELECT AUDIT_LOG_FILTER_SET_USER('test_user', 'conn_attempt_filter'); For versions earlier than 4.2.4: The above functions are not supported. Use the auditing features available in that version to capture successful and failed connection attempts.

title: Ensure 'FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS' Is Less than or Equal to '5'
description: The FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS setting determines how many failed login attempts are permitted before the system locks the user's account. While different profiles can have different and more restrictive settings, such as USERS, the minimum(s) recommended here should be set on the DEFAULT profile. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Oracle-mode tenant. Passes when the DEFAULT profile FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS is 5 or less (UNLIMITED fails). Runs obclient against an Oracle-mode tenant using the connection options in OB_ORA_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uSYS@oracle"); supply the password via OB_ORA_CONN (-p...) or ~/.my.cnf.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1.1 Ensure 'FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS' Is Less than or Equal to '5'

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_ORA_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uSYS@oracle} -N -B -e "SELECT CASE WHEN LIMIT NOT IN ('UNLIMITED', 'DEFAULT') AND TO_NUMBER(LIMIT) <= 5 THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END FROM SYS.DBA_PROFILES WHERE PROFILE = 'DEFAULT' AND RESOURCE_NAME = 'FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: ALTER PROFILE DEFAULT LIMIT FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS 5; (and for every other profile in use).

title: Ensure 'PASSWORD_LIFE_TIME' Is LESS than or Equal to '365'
description: The PASSWORD_LIFE_TIME setting determines how long a password may be used before the user is required to be change it. The suggested value for this is 365 days or less.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1.3 Ensure 'PASSWORD_LIFE_TIME' Is LESS than or Equal to '365'

audit.command: In the Oracle-mode tenant run SELECT PROFILE, RESOURCE_NAME, LIMIT FROM SYS.DBA_PROFILES WHERE PROFILE = 'DEFAULT' AND RESOURCE_NAME = 'PASSWORD_LIFE_TIME'; The value must be 365 (days) or less; UNLIMITED is a finding. Check other profiles in use the same way.

remediation.command: Remediate this setting by executing the following SQL statement for each PROFILE returned by the audit procedure. ALTER PROFILE <profile_name> LIMIT PASSWORD_LIFE_TIME 365;

title: Ensure 'PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION' Is Set for All Profiles
description: The PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION determines password settings requirements when a user password is changed at the SQL command prompt. It should be set for all profiles.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1.5 Ensure 'PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION' Is Set for All Profiles

audit.command: In the Oracle-mode tenant run SELECT PROFILE, RESOURCE_NAME, LIMIT FROM SYS.DBA_PROFILES WHERE RESOURCE_NAME = 'PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION'; Every profile must name a valid password verification function; NULL (the default) is a finding.

remediation.command: Create a custom password verification function which fulfills the password requirements of the organization. ALTER PROFILE <profile_name> LIMIT PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION <password_verify_func>; It is recommended that the password verification feature implement the following requirements to meet security standards: - Passwords must be at least 14 characters long.

title: Minimum Privileges
description: The unnecessary privileges should be revoked from user to minimize security risks and adhere to the principle of least privilege.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.2.2 Minimum Privileges

audit.command: To assess this recommendation, execute the following SQL statement. SELECT * FROM DBA_SYS_PRIVS; SELECT * FROM DBA_ROLE_PRIVS; SELECT * FROM USER_TAB_PRIVS; The returned user's privileges should address the needs of the organization, should not have unnecessary or excessive system, role, or object permissions.

remediation.command: Remediate this setting by executing the following SQL statement: REVOKE <role> FROM <username>; REVOKE <system_privilege> FROM <username>; REVOKE <operation_privilege> on <object> FROM <username>;

title: Ensure 'AUDIT_SYS_OPERATIONS' is set to TRUE
description: The AUDIT_SYS_OPERATIONS setting provides for the auditing of all user activities conducted under the SYS accounts. The setting should be set to TRUE to enable this auditing. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Oracle-mode tenant, using the benchmark query. Passes when audit_sys_operations is TRUE on every server. Runs obclient against an Oracle-mode tenant using the connection options in OB_ORA_CONN (default "-h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uSYS@oracle"); supply the password via OB_ORA_CONN (-p...) or ~/.my.cnf.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.2 Ensure 'AUDIT_SYS_OPERATIONS' is set to TRUE

audit.command: out=$(obclient ${OB_ORA_CONN:--h127.0.0.1 -P2881 -uSYS@oracle} -N -B -e "SELECT svr_ip, name, value FROM oceanbase.GV\$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name = 'audit_sys_operations'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk -F'\t' 'NF >= 3 {n++; if (toupper($3) != "TRUE") b++} END {print (n > 0 && b == 0) ? "compliant" : "noncompliant"}'

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET AUDIT_SYS_OPERATIONS = TRUE;

title: Enable Audit Options According to Requirements
description: Enabling the audit option causes auditing of any attempt, successful or not to do database operations. For auditing requests, audit rule should be configured to align with specific requirements.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.3 Enable Audit Options According to Requirements

audit.command: In the Oracle-mode tenant review SELECT * FROM SYS.ALL_DEF_AUDIT_OPTS; SELECT * FROM SYS.DBA_STMT_AUDIT_OPTS; and SELECT * FROM SYS.DBA_OBJ_AUDIT_OPTS; The views must show auditing enabled for the critical and high-risk statements and objects your policy requires; an empty view or missing high-risk activities is a finding.

remediation.command: To remediate this setting, execute one of the following SQL statements. 1. Audit specified statement operation: AUDIT <statement_operation> BY <username> WHENEVER [NOT] SUCCESSFUL; 2. Audit specified operations on a specififed database object: AUDIT <object_operations> ON <obj_name> | ON DEFAULT;

title: Enable Automatic Major Compaction before Backup
description: Automatic major compaction should be enabled before the backup is scheduled.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.2 Enable Automatic Major Compaction before Backup

audit.command: Review the backup configuration for each OceanBase tenant to confirm that automatic major compaction is enabled as part of the backup policy: - If the OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP) is used, examine the tenant-level backup settings within OCP and verify that the option to enable automatic major compaction (or equivalent setting related to compaction triggering during backup) is activated.

remediation.command: Ensure that automatic major compaction is enabled for all tenants that are configured for backup: - When using OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP), update the tenant's backup policy to include automatic major compaction as a prerequisite step. - In environments managed without OCP, work with database administrators to configure the system to trigger major compaction automatically prior to backup execution, in accordance with OceanBase best practices.

title: Ensure 'PASSWORD_LOCK_TIME' Is Greater than or Equal to '1'
description: The PASSWORD_LOCK_TIME setting determines how many days must pass for the user's account to be unlocked after the set number of failed login attempts has occurred. The suggested value for this is one day or greater.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1.2 Ensure 'PASSWORD_LOCK_TIME' Is Greater than or Equal to '1'

audit.command: In the Oracle-mode tenant run SELECT PROFILE, RESOURCE_NAME, LIMIT FROM SYS.DBA_PROFILES WHERE PROFILE = 'DEFAULT' AND RESOURCE_NAME = 'PASSWORD_LOCK_TIME'; The value must be 1 (day) or greater; check other profiles in use the same way.

remediation.command: Remediate this setting by executing the following SQL statement for each PROFILE returned by the audit procedure. ALTER PROFILE <profile_name> LIMIT PASSWORD_LOCK_TIME 1;

title: Ensure 'PASSWORD_GRACE_TIME' Is LESS than or Equal to '5'
description: The PASSWORD_GRACE_TIME setting determines how many days can pass after the user's password expires before the user's login capability is automatically locked out. The suggested value for this is five days or less.
reference: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1.4 Ensure 'PASSWORD_GRACE_TIME' Is LESS than or Equal to '5'

audit.command: In the Oracle-mode tenant run SELECT PROFILE, RESOURCE_NAME, LIMIT FROM SYS.DBA_PROFILES WHERE PROFILE = 'DEFAULT' AND RESOURCE_NAME = 'PASSWORD_GRACE_TIME'; The value must be 5 (days) or less; UNLIMITED is a finding. Check other profiles in use the same way.

remediation.command: Remediate this setting by executing the following SQL statement for each PROFILE returned by the audit procedure. ALTER PROFILE <profile_name> LIMIT PASSWORD_GRACE_TIME 5;
